safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(الله) the majestic name is a second mubtadaʾ [Note: if the pronoun (هو) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).. or the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو) if the pronoun refers to the god worshipped about whom the Messenger, peace be upon him, was asked.], (أحد) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله) [Note: or a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو.
(3, 4) or resumptive, within the scope of the saying.], (له) is attached to the khabar of يكن: (كفوا).
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «هو الله أحد ... » is in the position of accusative, the thing said.
And the clause: «الله أحد ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو.
And the clause: «الله الصمد ... » is in the position of nominative, a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو «3».
And the clause: «لم يلد ... » is in the position of nominative, a third khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو «4».
And the clause: «لم يولد ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لم يلد.
And the clause: «لم يكن له كفوا أحد» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لم يلد.

* Morphology:
(الصمد): a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective); its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas, in the sense of مفعول, i.e. the one to whom needs are directed.
(كفوا): a noun meaning "equal"; its wazn is فعل with two ḍammas, and the wāw is a lightening of the hamza.

* Rhetoric:
1- Concision (ījāz): in His saying, the Exalted: «هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ»:
This verse contains two of the names of Allah the Exalted, which comprise all attributes of perfection, namely al-Aḥad and al-Ṣamad, because they indicate the oneness of the holy Essence described with all attributes of perfection. The explanation is that al-Aḥad conveys His particular existence in which none other shares, and al-Ṣamad conveys all attributes of perfection, because lordship ends with Him, so He is the point to which requests return, from Him and to Him. This is not complete in reality except for the one who has gathered all attributes of perfection, and that is fitting only for Allah the Exalted.
2- Fronting (taqdīm): in His saying, the Exalted: «وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ».
Here He fronted the adverbial phrase, whereas in eloquent Arabic speech it is to be put later and not fronted. So what of it being fronted in the most eloquent and clearest speech? The reason is that the speech was only driven to negate equality from the Essence of the Creator, glory be to Him, and the focus and centre of this meaning is this adverbial phrase, so it was the most important and most concerning thing, and the most deserving and fitting of fronting.

* Benefits:
- The merit of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ:
On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him: A man heard another man reciting: (قل هو الله أحد). In the morning, he came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, as the man thought it little. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, it equals a third of the Qur'an. In another report he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions: Is any of you unable to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night? That was hard on them and they said: Which of us can do that? He said: (قل هو الله أحد) is a third of the Qur'an. On the authority of Abū al-Dardāʾ that the Prophet ﷺ said: Allah divided the Qur'an into three parts, and made (قل هو الله أحد) one part of the Qur'an.
